messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE: gpu-serving-prod queue depth > 15k and HPA not scaling. Observed sustained token generation latency > 10s, many requests queued/throttled. Prometheus -> metrics-adapter showing errors (5xx). Impact: multiple customers reporting timeouts. Oncall: samantha (oncall) assigned.

samantha (oncall): seeing it. UI shows burst of traffic ~09:02 UTC and pool usage hit 100%. HPA events show repeated 'failed to get external metric'.

raj (eng-sre): looking at k8s. Can you paste `kubectl describe hpa gpu-inference -n prod` and `kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l k8s-app=metrics-adapter -o wide`?

samantha (oncall): grabbing output now.

samantha (oncall): ```
Name: gpu-inference
Namespace: prod
Labels: app=gpu-inference
Annotations: autoscaling.alpha.kubernetes.io/behavior: ...
Min replicas: 2
Max replicas: 20
Metrics: ( current / target )
  external/prometheus/custom_gpu_queue  12k / 500
Events:
  Type    Reason             Age   From                       Message
  ----    ------             ----  ----                       -------
  Warning FailedGetMetrics   2m    horizontal-pod-autoscaler  failed to get external metrics: unable to query metrics API: 500 Internal Server Error
```

lina (eng-runtime): metrics-adapter logs are noisy, getting 500s upstream from Prometheus throttle/timeout. Might be scrape backlog.

raj (eng-sre): `kubectl logs deployment/metrics-adapter -n kube-system --since=30m` (tail):

samantha (oncall): ```
E0309 09:05:12.342 adapter.go:198] error fetching external metrics: error querying prometheus: context deadline exceeded
E0309 09:05:13.103 adapter.go:201] error fetching external metrics: 500 "server error: query timeout"
W0309 09:06:00.001 adapter.go:150] Prometheus scrape lag detected: last scrape 4m ago for job=gpu-exporter
```

tom (eng-ml): customer-facing insight: queues back up because autoscaler can't see the custom metric 'gpu_queue_length' — if the HPA can't fetch metric it won't scale. We need manual scale to avoid customer impact while fixing metrics pipeline.

sofia (support): several customers flagged timeouts in last 10m, including a high-value enterprise. Notified sales. Need ETA for mitigation.

raj (eng-sre): plan: 1) temporarily scale deployment to relieve queue 2) bump HPA maxReplicas to allow rapid autoscale once metrics recover 3) triage Prometheus/adapter (restart adapter & investigate Prometheus query timeouts) 4) add short-lived fallback: route low-priority traffic to hosted API tier.

lina (eng-runtime): executing step 3 now. I'll restart metrics-adapter and metrics-server sequentially to clear transient error state. Will also check Prometheus TSDB disk pressure.

samantha (oncall): doing step 1/2: 
```bash
kubectl scale deployment gpu-pool -n prod --replicas=18
kubectl patch hpa gpu-inference -n prod -p '{"spec":{"maxReplicas":50}}'
```
Scaling command returned success. GPU pool currently provisioning nodes; expected warmup ~2-4m.

deploy-bot: Started provisioning 6 additional GPU nodes (request id: prov-ccbf12). Estimated ready 3m.

raj (eng-sre): verify HPA events again after adapter restart. If adapter still 500ing, HPA will remain stuck. Lina, please paste adapter restart output and quick health check.

lina (eng-runtime): restarted metrics-adapter and metrics-server. Adapter health endpoint now returns 200. Quick PromQL check: `sum(gpu_queue_length) by(instance)` returns 16000 -> appears available.

samantha (oncall): re-check HPA: `kubectl describe hpa gpu-inference -n prod` shows metric now visible: `external/prometheus/custom_gpu_queue  16k / 500` but HPA is throttled by scale limits on cluster? getting events: `Failed rescale: scale rate limit exceeded` and `insufficient quota` occasionally.

raj (eng-sre): cluster autoscaler logs show we're at per-AZ max for GPU nodes from cloud provider side. Could explain inability to add more GPUs even though we scaled deployment. Asking infra to request burst capacity or temporarily move pods to another region?

lina (eng-runtime): but new pods were scheduled on existing nodes with kube-scheduler using taints/tolerations; some pods pending with `0/24 nodes are available: Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu`.

tom (eng-ml): mitigation idea: spin up lower-memory quantized model replica set that uses fewer GPUs and route a fraction of traffic to it to reduce pressure. That buys time for infra to increase capacity. I can stand one up in ~8-12m.

sofia (support): I told the high-value customer we're investigating and applied an incident status banner (ETA ~30m). They'll escalate if no perf improvement.

raj (eng-sre): next steps executed: - manual scale to 18 replicas (partial relief) - HPA maxReplicas bumped to 50 - metrics-adapter restarted and now returning metrics - infra team engaged for GPU capacity bump (ticket #INFRA-4421) - tom to stage quantized fallback

lina (eng-runtime): digging into root cause: Prometheus had a spike in scrape backlog due to slow queries from eval jobs hitting TSDB; disk IO saturated for 2m leading adapter queries to time out. We need to tune Prometheus query concurrency and add read replicas for heavy queries.

samantha (oncall): handing on-call to raj for longer-term mitigation at 09:45 UTC — I'm pausing noise and moving to coordination with SOC/sales. Raj, take the remaining incident ops. :handshake:

raj (eng-sre): taking over. I'll coordinate infra and runtime. Lina, prioritize: 1) add Prometheus query limiter + read-only replica or Thanos querier fallback, 2) ensure adapter uses query timeouts and retries that don't cascade.

lina (eng-runtime): got it. Implementing query limiter now (small config change). Also enable metrics-adapter caching for 30s to reduce query load. Will monitor.

tom (eng-ml): quantized fallback replica set up in canary and I've routed 20% of low-priority traffic to it. Early results: queue decreased ~30% for GPU pool. No regressions in quality in quick checks.

sofia (support): customers reporting improved responsiveness for some traffic. Will update incident banner to 'degraded' -> 'partial mitigation achieved'.

raj (eng-sre): infra responded: cloud provider approved temporary quota bump, provisioning nodes now. Expect full capacity restoration in 6-10m.

deploy-bot: Provisioning completed: 6 GPU nodes added, kube node registration complete.

raj (eng-sre): now that nodes are up and adapter healthy, HPA observed scale events and is increasing replica count automatically. Monitoring latency and queue.

samantha (oncall): thanks all. I'm leaving notes in the incident doc and will follow up on customer comms. Moving to post-incident for runbook updates: add Prometheus query limiter, adapter caching, and a playbook for burst-capacity requests.

lina (eng-runtime): opening PRs for runbook and config changes. Will schedule a follow-up to add a read-replica path for Prometheus.

tom (eng-ml): will create a template for fast quantized fallback deploys so we can route traffic automatically next time.

sofia (support): tracking customer comms and will attach logs/metrics for the affected tenants to the ticket.

raj (eng-sre): incident state: mitigated -> queues draining, HPA functioning, manual patches applied (revert plan pending). I will keep monitoring for 45m then start rollback of manual scale and HPA max once stable.

samantha (oncall): final note: incident duration ~1h10m from first page to mitigation. Root causes: Prometheus query overload -> metrics-adapter timeouts -> HPA unable to read external metric -> GPU pool exhausted -> autoscale blocked by cloud quota. Follow-ups assigned. :white_check_mark:

sofia (support): adding affected customer list to incident ticket and prepping postmortem distribution.

raj (eng-sre): handing back to samantha for incident close paperwork. Thanks team.

samantha (oncall): closing the live coordination channel, will create postmortem doc and link in this thread. Good recovery, everyone. :slightly_smiling_face:
